name: AsyncGenerator
doc: ABC for asynchronous generator classes that implement the protocol defined in PEP 525 and PEP 492.

name: AsyncIterable
doc: ABC for classes that provide an __aiter__ method. See also the definition of asynchronous iterable.

name: AsyncIterator
doc: ABC for classes that provide __aiter__ and __anext__ methods. See also the definition of asynchronous iterator.

name: Awaitable
doc: ABC for awaitable objects, which can be used in await expressions. Custom implementations must provide the __await__() method.

name: Buffer
doc: ABC for classes that provide the __buffer__() method, implementing the buffer protocol. See PEP 688.

name: ByteString
doc:
Deprecated ABC serving as a common supertype of ``bytes`` and ``bytearray``.

This ABC is scheduled for removal in Python 3.17.
Use ``isinstance(obj, collections.abc.Buffer)`` to test if ``obj``
implements the buffer protocol at runtime. For use in type annotations,
either use ``Buffer`` or a union that explicitly specifies the types your
code supports (e.g., ``bytes | bytearray | memoryview``).

deprecated.text: The ByteString ABC has been deprecated. Use isinstance(obj, collections.abc.Buffer) to test if obj implements the buffer protocol at runtime. For use in type annotations, either use Buffer or a union that explicitly specifies the types your code supports (e.g., bytes | bytearray | memoryview). ByteString was originally intended to be an abstract class that would serve as a supertype of both bytes and bytearray. However, since the ABC never had any methods, knowing that an object was an instance of ByteString never actually told you anything useful about the object. Other common buffer types such as memoryview were also never understood as subtypes of ByteString (either at runtime or by static type checkers). See PEP 688 for more details.

name: index
doc:
S.index(value, [start, [stop]]) -> integer -- return first index of
value.  Raises ValueError if the value is not present.

Supporting start and stop arguments is optional, but
recommended.

changed.text: The index() method gained support for the stop and start arguments.

name: Callable
doc: ABC for classes that provide the __call__() method.

name: Collection
doc: ABC for sized iterable container classes.

name: Container
doc: ABC for classes that provide the __contains__() method.

name: Coroutine
doc: ABC for coroutine compatible classes. These implement the following methods, defined in Coroutine Objects: send(), throw(), and close(). Custom implementations must also implement __await__(). All Coroutine instances are also instances of Awaitable.

name: Generator
doc: ABC for generator classes that implement the protocol defined in PEP 342 that extends iterators with the send(), throw() and close() methods.

name: Hashable
doc: ABC for classes that provide the __hash__() method.

name: ItemsView
doc: ABCs for mapping, items, keys, and values views.

name: Iterable
doc: ABC for classes that provide the __iter__() method.

name: Iterator
doc: ABC for classes that provide the __iter__() and __next__() methods. See also the definition of iterator.

name: KeysView
doc: ABCs for mapping, items, keys, and values views.

name: Mapping
doc:
A Mapping is a generic container for associating key/value
pairs.

This class provides concrete generic implementations of all
methods except for __getitem__, __iter__, and __len__.

name: MappingView
doc: ABCs for mapping, items, keys, and values views.

name: MutableMapping
doc:
A MutableMapping is a generic container for associating
key/value pairs.

This class provides concrete generic implementations of all
methods except for __getitem__, __setitem__, __delitem__,
__iter__, and __len__.

name: MutableSequence
doc:
All the operations on a read-write sequence.

Concrete subclasses must provide __new__ or __init__,
__getitem__, __setitem__, __delitem__, __len__, and insert().

name: MutableSet
doc:
A mutable set is a finite, iterable container.

This class provides concrete generic implementations of all
methods except for __contains__, __iter__, __len__,
add(), and discard().

To override the comparisons (presumably for speed, as the
semantics are fixed), all you have to do is redefine __le__ and
then the other operations will automatically follow suit.

name: Reversible
doc: ABC for iterable classes that also provide the __reversed__() method.

name: Sequence
doc:
All the operations on a read-only sequence.

Concrete subclasses must override __new__ or __init__,
__getitem__, and __len__.

name: Set
doc:
A set is a finite, iterable container.

This class provides concrete generic implementations of all
methods except for __contains__, __iter__ and __len__.

To override the comparisons (presumably for speed, as the
semantics are fixed), redefine __le__ and __ge__,
then the other operations will automatically follow suit.

name: Sized
doc: ABC for classes that provide the __len__() method.

name: ValuesView
doc: ABCs for mapping, items, keys, and values views.
